note: Cached demo reasoning for the FALLBACK Seattle smoke spike (peak PM2.5 176, Sep 19 morning). Used when no LLM keys are set or live calls fail. UI labels this Demo cache.
research:
• Afternoon practice in orange/red air can trigger coughing and wheeze, especially for asthma — coaches often move it indoors above 150 AQI.
• Smoke particles are tiny enough to get deep into lungs, so bandanas do little; N95/KN95-style masks actually filter them.
• Poor sleep and foggy focus are common on multi-day smoke stretches — plan lighter homework blocks. Follow local officials, not apps.
plan:
1. Text your coach tonight: ask if tomorrow's practice moves indoors or shifts earlier before the plume peaks.
2. Pack a real mask (N95/KN95) in your bag and keep bus-stop waiting short — check the hourly dip around late afternoon.
3. Build a 10-minute box-fan + furnace-filter purifier for your bedroom and run it on low overnight.
4. Check on one person: grandparent, neighbor, or teammate with asthma — share the evening all-clear time.
critic:
• Forecasts shift: wind can clear this plume 6 hours early or trap it another day — this plan expires fast.
• Your block may differ 2x from the city sensor near a highway, hill, or valley — hyperlocal air varies.
• Generic plans ignore personal risk: asthma, heart conditions, and pregnancy change everything. Lesson: use apps to prepare early, but let officials and your doctor make the call.
